To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The concentrations of dissolved Cd, Cu, Zn and Fe in the water of the Rio Tint-Huelva Ría system were elevated.

the metal behaviour in a river-estuary system impacted by acid mine effluent was dominated by non-conservative behaviour of dissolved metals in the low salinities, with the turbidity maximum acting as a sink.
the metal behaviour in the estuarine system was dominated by the behaviour of dissolved metals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the behaviour of trace metals in the estuary of the Rio Tintio in south-west Spain.
the effects of acid drainage on estuarial metal chemistry and the behaviour of metals in estuaries impacted by acid mine water.
the role of particulates in the transport and distribution of trace metals in estuaries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dissolved metal concentrations were the dominant source of metal in the water and were the main cause of the observed non-conservative behaviour.
the behaviour of metals in this estuary is determined by the low pH of the water column.
acid mine drainage is not a source of particulate Cd, Zn and Cu in this estuary.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metals in acid mine drainage are transported as dissolved species and, in the low salinty region, are not removed from the water column.
the metal concentrations in the water samples were elevated, dissolved Cd and Cu behaved non-conservativly on each transect but dissolved Zn behaved conservatively.
the dissolved metal behaviour in the estuary is controlled by the low pH and the associated low metal solubility, rather than the high concentrations of suspended particulate matter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the behaviour of metals is dominated by their speciation and the chemical properties of the particulates.
the behaviour of metals in estuaries impacted by acid mine discharge is controlled by the chemistry of the water and not by adsorption processes on suspended particulate matter.

the behaviour of dissolved metals in the estuarine environment can be understood in terms of a simple model in which the metal is adsorbed on the suspended particulate material, which is then resuspended and transported down the estuary.
